analysis.evidence: The feminine singular verb agrees with הַיּוֹנָה, “the dove.” אֵלָיו, “to him,” identifies Noah as the one the dove came to, and לְעֵת עֶרֶב places her arrival in the evening.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: הַיּוֹנָה is the subject of the feminine singular verb וַתָּבֹא. The dove returns to Noah with an olive leaf בְּפִיהָ, “in her beak.”
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: In לְעֵת עֶרֶב, עֶרֶב specifies the time of day when the dove came back to Noah. The phrase means “at evening.”
analysis.morphology: Temporal preposition לְ prefixed to a common noun in the singular construct, of common gender.

analysis.evidence: In לְעֵת עֶרֶב, עֶרֶב specifies the time of the dove’s return to Noah. It came back in the evening.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After the dove returns, וְהִנֵּה introduces what Noah sees in its mouth, an olive leaf. That sight leads him to conclude that the waters have receded.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the presentative particle הִנֵּה.
analysis.sense: and there was (what one sees or finds)

analysis.evidence: עֲלֵה is in construct with זַיִת, forming עֲלֵה זַיִת, ‘an olive leaf’. בְּפִיהָ places the leaf in the dove’s mouth.
In עֲלֵה זַיִת, “a leaf of an olive tree,” זַיִת is the absolute noun following the construct עֲלֵה. It identifies the tree from which the dove’s leaf came.
analysis.morphology: Noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עֲלֵה זַיִת טָרָף בְּפִיהָ, טָרָף agrees with עֲלֵה, the masculine singular head of the phrase meaning “olive leaf.” It describes the condition of the leaf the dove carries in her beak.

draft.change: Clarify in the article summary that Genesis 8:11 illustrates holding something in the mouth. The verse already appears as defining evidence under mouth-body.
draft.definition: The physical mouth, here the beak in which a bird holds something.
draft.evidence: Genesis 8:11 describes the dove returning with an olive leaf בְּפִיהָ, in her beak.

analysis.evidence: The suffix ־הָ refers to הַיּוֹנָה, the dove. When she returns, בְּפִיהָ tells where the plucked olive leaf is: she holds it in her beak.
analysis.morphology: Locative preposition בְּ־ “in” + פִי, the masculine singular construct form of פֶּה + third-person feminine singular possessive suffix ־הָ “her”.
analysis.sense: Physical mouth of a person or animal.

analysis.evidence: The olive leaf in the dove’s beak gives Noah the evidence. The כִּי clause states what he knew from it: the waters had receded from the earth.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ
analysis.sense: to know that something is the case

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּדַע נֹחַ, “Noah knew,” נֹחַ is the subject of וַיֵּדַע. The dove returns to him with an olive leaf, and he recognizes that the waters have receded.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After וַיֵּדַע נֹחַ (“Noah knew”), כִּי introduces what Noah knew: the waters had receded from the earth.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: קַלּוּ agrees with its plural subject הַמַּיִם, “the waters.” From the olive leaf in the dove’s beak, Noah knew that the waters had receded from the surface of the earth.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural

analysis.evidence: In קַלּוּ הַמַּיִם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל locates the waters over the earth, and מֵ־ marks their recession from that position.
analysis.morphology: Preposition עַל with prefixed מִן in the form מֵ־.

analysis.evidence: The olive leaf in the dove’s mouth tells Noah that the waters have receded. In מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ, the ground is the surface the floodwaters had covered.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, of common gender, with the prefixed definite article הָ־.
